name: OKC Will Rogers World Airport
before:
Oklahoma's busiest commercial airport, about 6 miles south west of downtown Oklahoma City. Southwest carries the most passengers here, with a market share of nearly 48 per cent as of April 2022, and the airport had its busiest year on record in 2019 at nearly 4.42 million passengers.

The important recent change: international flights only began on 8 November 2025, after a new customs facility opened earlier that year. Until then this was a domestic airport, so any older guidance about international service is out of date.

The name changed too. It was Will Rogers World Airport until 2024, the only airport anywhere to use World in its designation, and is now Will Rogers International. Locally it is still just Will Rogers.

The terminal dates from a 110 million dollar rebuild begun in 2001, which demolished the old twin concourses and replaced them with integrated concourses under high ceilings.

The naming has a sad symmetry. Will Rogers died in a plane crash in Alaska in 1935 alongside the pilot Wiley Post, and Oklahoma City's other airport is named after Post.
after:
Oklahoma's busiest commercial airport, about 6 miles south west of downtown Oklahoma City. Southwest carries the most passengers here, and the airport handled 4.6 million passengers in 2024.

International flights are new here: American Airlines now flies a seasonal nonstop to Cancún. Any older guidance saying the airport has no international service is out of date.

The name has changed too: it was Will Rogers World Airport and is now OKC Will Rogers International. Locally it is often just Will Rogers.

Will Rogers died in a plane crash in Alaska in 1935 alongside the pilot Wiley Post, and the city's Wiley Post Airport is named after Post.

claims.note: Was 'the airport had its busiest year on record in 2019 at nearly 4.42 million passengers', now overtaken. The city's 4.6 million is TOTAL passengers, arriving and departing. The FAA counts 2,243,575 revenue boardings in 2024 (boardings only, about half of total passengers), in line with it, and 2,242,888 in 2025, so 2025 was about the same. The operator's own monthly reports and its 2025 review are PDFs that refuse automated reads (403, and blank in the browser). No source calls 2024 a record in words, so the text does not.
